title: Raspberry Pi private data never constructs its std::string
summary: Category functional; severity medium; confidence high. Owner coordinator; open, nonblocking audit follow-up. Location: indigo_optional_drivers/ccd_rpi/indigo_ccd_rpi.cpp:1693-1694 and:1766; type:932-941 contains std::string eid. indigo_safe_malloc provides zeroed raw storage, not C++ construction, but attach immediately assigns to eid. This invokes a member of a non-live std::string, with implementation-dependent startup crash/invalid storage behavior. free at shutdown also skips the string destructor and can leak its heap allocation. Existing FND-000019–000027 cover different optional-driver failures, not this C++ lifetime mismatch. Use value-initializing new rpi_private_data{} and matching delete, or a deliberate placement-construction/destruction contract. Verify attach/detach with short and non-SSO camera IDs under a fake libcamera backend; Raspberry Pi/real libcamera unavailable in this read-only review. Next: coordinator assigns scoped remediation and regression verification; full evidence/remedy in findings.md (FM-2). No fix or risk acceptance claimed.
